incident_during_execution.summary: launchd-deployed daemon wedged on first post-hold admission: main-thread blocked in host::verify_volume -> fs::read_to_string(sentinel) -> open() on an external volume (/Volumes/UOR-Workspace quarantine-mounted APFS, or /Volumes/X10 Pro exFAT-fskit), reproducibly across debug and release binaries and across restarts, while identical reads succeed from shell context. Foreground (shell-context) execution of the same release daemon admitted and finalized the reserved job cleanly, proving the repaired code and the admission path. Diagnosis: OS-level consent evaluation (TCC removable-volume / Gatekeeper) for the new unsigned binary's cdhash under the launchd bootstrap context; the prior binary's cdhash held an existing grant.
incident_during_execution.evidence: two `sample` stacks identical at verify_volume->read_to_string->open; sentinels readable from shell (stat sizes 46/47/45); codesign identical ad-hoc on all three binaries; bytemuck-popup diagnosis documents the same syspolicyd prompt-block class on the restored volume
incident_during_execution.unblock: Owner grants the OS consent for the new binary (pending prompt on screen, or System Settings > Privacy & Security > Files and Folders / spctl rule). The launchd supervisor is re-deployed and recovers immediately on consent. Stopgap if consent is unavailable: run the supervisor from a consent-holding foreground context (proven), but that is unsupervised and session-bound.
incident_during_execution.follow_up: runner verify_volume has no timeout: a hung sentinel read wedges the daemon silently with no error or blocked record. Recommend a bounded read or explicit unavailable error so future wedges surface as admission-blocked instead of a silent hang.
